analysis:
Examined all supplied metadata, patches and source excerpts. These units contain documentation, not executable implementation; no independently supported security regression was identified. Selected-model recovery adds automatic memory-driven loading and eviction (docs/architecture/hardware-support.md head 451–488, visible in the patch). Documented safeguards retain load accounting, selected-model protection, request/lease/pin exclusions, bounded backoff and victim rechecks. Add-on documentation explicitly extends the hold fence and cancellation to recovery and coordinator preloads (docs/architecture/addon-hold.md head 67–70), consistent with TB-012/T-059 and A-018. No supplied change alters credentials, serving authorization, encryption, cache scope or billing; T-041's persistence and isolation controls are not changed here.
Integration must verify ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift against load admission, eviction snapshots and enterAddonHold: cancellation must prevent slot publication, and request admission must not race victim retirement. The new pending-owner-review policy releases request-busy adopted models after ten minutes (changelog.d/selected-models-recover.md head 8); reconcile this with the hardware document's idle-victim description and verify that release blocks new requests while retaining in-flight ownership. The 15-second shutdown unload bound (same file head 7) also needs implementation review to distinguish process termination from falsely treating native cleanup as complete, particularly given hardware-support.md base 299–305 and 316–320. Relevant integration concerns are A-018, TB-007, T-010, T-028, T-029 and T-059; missing implementation is a coverage limit, not proof of a missing control. No threat-model expansion finding is established from documentation alone.
